Start at https://www.student.com/ and complete the following task by navigating within that website.

Find the lowest-priced Student housing near Liverpool International College which has been priced between 100 to 300 pounds and has a private bathroom.

Rules:
- Work entirely in this one browser tab. Do NOT open new tabs.
- Do NOT use a search engine (Google, Bing, etc.) or cached/archived copies (e.g. web.archive.org). Navigate the site itself, starting from https://www.student.com/.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

URLs require status and redirect verification before citation.] Matches in posts page 3: [{"id":9168,"date":"2017-05-26T15:55:31","date_gmt":"2017-05-26T15:55:31","guid":{"rendered":"https://www.student.com/?p=9168"},"modified":"2025-02-27T11:29:09","modified_gmt":"2025-02-27T11:29:09","slug":"best-student-areas-liverpool","status":"publish","type":"post","link":"https://www.student.com/articles/best-student-areas-liverpool","title":{"rendered":"4 Best Student Areas in Liverpool"},"content":{"rendered":"

If you’re looking to find out about the best student areas in Liverpool – this guide is for you! 

To help put this guide together, we spoke to two of our landlord partners, Meeta Padhiar from Galbraith Estates and Andrew Britton from iQ Student Accommodation.  

In no particular order, we’ve taken a look at the most popular areas and what makes them great.

Here are the four best student areas in Liverpool:

1. Wavertree

Wavertree is by far one of the most popular areas in Liverpool for students.

Because of its bustling student population, you’ll find plenty of shops, restaurants and bars here that offer great student deals.

An interesting fact about Wavertree is that its name comes from the Old English words ‘wæfre’ and ‘treow’, which mean “wavering tree”.

Needless to say, the area isn’t short of green spaces – like the Wavertree Botanic Gardens.

Meeta: “The popular, ever growing area of Wavertree consists of a diverse range of shops, restaurants and bars, right on your doorstep. It is nothing shy of culture and fun. A thriving local area catering for students living away from home. A great place to see, visit and spend time for both students and their families.”

Another highlight of Wavertree is that rents are, on average, cheaper than some of the more central areas in Liverpool.

If you don’t mind a 40 minute walk to university (20 minutes by bus), then you’ll love living in Wavertree.  

2. Liverpool University Area

Perhaps you’re not a huge fan of walking.

Well, fear not, there are plenty of accommodation options close to Liverpool’s universities.

What’s more, the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University are both reasonably close by.

So, if you’d like to live within walking distance of the city centre – this is the area for you!

Here, you’ll be close to sites like the World Museum, Walker Art Gallery and Central Library.

Liverpool Lime Street Station is just around the corner too!

Andrew: “The University of Liverpool city campus is a hive of activity where students can find most things they need, but there is so much more just a short walk away.”

Compare the best Liverpool student accommodation on Student.com.

3. Liverpool City Centre

Why not take full advantage of what Liverpool has to offer by living right in the city centre?

The majority of Liverpool’s shopping hotspots and famous landmarks are here – so chances are you’ll be in this area regularly.

Andrew: “In omission of the obvious tourist areas of the city, one area perfect for students is Bold Street where you’ll find dozens of unique retailers, world food stores, bars and restaurants most of which offer student discounts. On the streets running parallel to Bold Street in the Rope Walks District you can find many surprising hidden gems, including the FACT cinema and arts centre – definitely not your average cinema.”

The main drawback, as with any city centre location, is that rents here can be slightly higher compared to other areas.

4. Baltic Triangle

The Baltic Triangle is the place to be for creatives in Liverpool.  

The area is home to Liverpool’s creative businesses, as well as great restaurants, bars and live music venues.    

Living here, you’ll also find the city centre and areas like Chinatown within walking distance.  

Andrew: “The Baltic Triangle area of the city is fast becoming the cultural and creative centre of Liverpool with many of the old warehouse buildings undergoing transformation into conceptual venue spaces. Whatever you’re studying you’ll find something in the area that will inspire you!”

Check out our Liverpool student guide for tips on the best places to eat, shop and have fun.

Getting around

Liverpool has great transport options with a good network of buses, trains and ferries. The best place for information on routes, timetables, fares, passes and travel guides for Liverpool is the Merseytravel website. The site also regularly features special promotions and has a journey planner tool to help you navigate the city.

Cycling is a good way to get around and explore Liverpool, as well as being an excellent way to keep fit. Liverpool boasts the UK’s biggest bike hire service outside of London, Citybike, which offers 24-hour rentals from more than 130 stations across the city. Citybike also offers discounted student rates for their annual memberships and often run promotions at the start of university semesters.

Things to do

Liverpool was the European Capital of Culture in 2008 and is now a popular destination for visitors from around the world. From the Liverpool Echo Arena, a great venue for live music, to a fantastic sports scene, the city has so much for international students to experience.

If you’re keen to save money, there’s a wide range of activities on offer for free, or a very reasonable price.

Liverpool has more museums and galleries than any other UK city outside of London, and most of them are free to enter. A few of the most popular sites are the Museum of Liverpool, World Museum, Tate Liverpool and Walker Art Gallery – one of the oldest public art museums in the UK. For a full list of museums and galleries in Liverpool, check out the National Museums Liverpool website.

For music lovers, the Liverpool International Music Festival Summer Jam is a three-day outdoor music festival that attracts headline acts from around the world every year. The best thing about the festival is that it’s free to access!

Eating out

Liverpool is a great destination for passionate foodies. The city offers a diverse range of food options and some of the best international cuisine in the UK.

There are plenty of hidden gems dotted around the city and several areas that are popular with international students.

For some of the best Chinese restaurants in the UK, visit Liverpool’s Chinatown – home to one of the oldest overseas Chinese communities in Europe and almost 100 restaurants. Or for a truly picturesque dining experience, head over to the Albert Dock – a World Heritage Site waterfront featuring the UK’s largest collection of Grade I listed buildings.

Eating out doesn’t have to be pricey either. If you’re looking to eat out on a budget, there are plenty of inexpensive eats to sample in Liverpool. Here are a few recommendations to start you off on your gastronomic journey:

  • Bakchich

Bakchich offers Lebanese street food, a sensational blend of fresh and vibrant flavours. Perfect for both quick lunches and sit-down evening meals.

Address: 54 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4ER

  • Bellagio

Bellagio is one of the most popular places in Liverpool for traditional British fish and chips.

Address: Unit 15, The Colonnades, Albert Dock, Liverpool, L3 4AA

  • Big Bowl Noodle Bar

For a hearty bowl of noodles, Big Bowl Noodle Bar, as the name suggests, is the place to visit.

Address: 54 Berry Street, Liverpool, L1 4JF

  • Café Tabac

Café Tabac offers a cool, continental mix of coffee, cocktails and cinema, and a great selection of European food.

Address: 126 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4JA

  • Delkery

Delkery is a friendly, family-run café that serves fresh and quality handmade food and drinks.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • The Egg Café

The Egg Café is one of Liverpool’s best vegetarian and vegan restaurants. It’s located in a quaint old Victorian Warehouse and also serves as an independent art gallery.

Address: Top Floor, 16 – 18 Newington, Liverpool, L1 4ED

  • Lox & Caper

Located in the Merseyside Youth Association building, Lox & Caper has a great selection of good value food, all of which is prepared in-house.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • Tortilla

While Tortilla isn’t exclusive to Liverpool, it’s an excellent place for inexpensive tortillas and offers student discount.

Address: 70 Lord Street, Liverpool, L2 1TL

Shopping

For an ‘everything under one roof’ experience, check out Liverpool ONE. Liverpool ONE is the largest shopping complex in the city centre and the fifth largest in the UK. It’s host to a great selection of more than 170 shops, restaurants and bars and entertainment facilities.

Other shopping complexes worth checking out in Liverpool’s city centre are Metquarter Liverpool and St. Johns Shopping Centre.

Another shopping hotspot, especially for visitors is Liverpool’s Bold Street. Along the bustling high street, you’ll discover a range of boutiques and independent shops, as well as a mixture of big brand names.

Finding accommodation 

Finding a place to live in Liverpool can be daunting, especially if you’re looking from overseas.

The most popular areas are the City Centre, Wavertree, Liverpool University Area and the Baltic Triangle. As with most cities, average prices for accommodation in the city centre tend to be slightly higher than other areas.

Want to know more? Read our guide on the best student areas in Liverpool.

For the best selection of quality student accommodation in Liverpool, visit Student.com.

Liverpool is a great city for university students. It’s a fun city with lots of interesting things to do, and most importantly for prospective students, it’s home to a couple of very good universities. If you’re looking for cheap student accommodation in Liverpool then you can start your search on this website or on our app. Make sure to also sign-up for a free account. This way a member of our bookings team can help you find the ideal student home just for you.

One of the good things about Liverpool, compared to for example London, is that student accommodation is much cheaper on average. You can find some really good student properties that won’t break the bank but are still in good locations, near universities and the city centre. In this post we’ve listed some of the most popular options for cheap student accommodation in Liverpool.

Atlantic Point

Atlantic Point is in a great location near the city centre. This means you’ll have great shopping and nightlife options right at your doorstep, in addition to being able to get to your campus quickly. Especially the Liverpool John Moores University city campus is really close by, just a 5-minute walk away. In Atlantic Point you’ll live in a private en-suite room, meaning you’ll have a bedroom and a bathroom just for yourself. The rooms are fully furnished and the property facilities include an entertainment room, a communal laundry room and bike storage. Prices start from £107/week.

Grand Central

As the name suggests, you’ll be in a very central location at the Grand Central. Just over a 5-minute walk to Liverpool John Moores University and about 15 minutes on foot to the University of Liverpool, you’ll also be right next to Liverpool Lime Street and Liverpool Central stations. Grand Central is equipped with airy rooms, fresh decor and laundry facilities, meaning you can quickly make this place feel like a home when you study in Liverpool. There are several options for how you want to live, with private rooms with shared bathrooms, private rooms with en-suite bathroom and fully self-contained studio apartments all on offer. Prices start from £105/week.

Agnes Jones House

Located in Liverpool’s Georgian Quarter, Agnes Jones House is about a 10-minute walk from both the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University. With prices starting at just £85/week, this is the perfect property for a student looking for a cheap, convenient home away from home at university. With an entertainment room, bike storage and laundry, everything you need is on-site.

St Andrew’s Gardens

St Andrew’s Gardens is the cheapest accommodation we currently list in Liverpool, with prices starting at just £84/week. Even at this price you’ll still be within walking distance of your campus. You can walk to Liverpool John Moores University in about 5 minutes and to the University of Liverpool in 10 minutes. You’ll get to live in a private bedroom, and depending on the room you choose, your bathroom can be either shared or private. All bills are included in the price as well.

Falkland House

Falkland House has a great location near the Royal Liverpool University Hospital. You can walk to Liverpool John Moores University in 10 minutes and to the University of Liverpool in under 15. The rooms are fully furnished and all bills, including Wi-Fi, are included in the rent. The facilities include a bike storage, entertainment room and communal laundry. You’ll also be in a safe environment with an onsite manager and a security officer always on-site. Prices start from £118/week.

All prices are correct as of 15th February 2023. For full details please refer to the property page listing on Student.com or contact a member of the team for confirmation of pricing. Our bookings team are always happy to answer any questions you may have and help you find the ideal student home for you.

Liverpool is home to Liverpool F.C. and Everton F.C. and is one of the most passionate football cities in the country. Both Liverpool and Everton are historically successful clubs with Liverpool having claimed 19 English league titles and six Champions League titles, and Everton having been champions of England nine times. Especially Liverpool is one of the most widely supported teams in the world, with lots of fans in all corners of the globe.

Liverpool, hometown of the legendary Beatles, is a city and metropolitan borough in Merseyside, England. This iconic city has a lot more to offer than football and one of the most influential bands of all time though. With a grand backdrop of Victorian and Georgian buildings, it’s an intimate and vibrant city that celebrates its glorious past. It’s home to many famous landmarks such as the homes of The Beatles members, The Liver Buildings, and the historic docks – all of which will become familiar sights if you choose to study in the city.

Still, for a football fan, the beautiful game is definitely one of the biggest draws of the city. In this post we list some great options for student accommodation for anyone who’s coming to study in Liverpool and is interested in seeing some games.

Student accommodation near Anfield

Anfield is one of the most legendary stadiums in the world. The team’s passionate fans, The Kop stand behind one of the goals and the singing of You’ll Never Walk Alone before every home game are things every football fan knows about. Liverpool has tens of millions of fans all over the world and it was 7th in the Deloitte Football Money League in 2022, meaning it is the 7th richest football club in the world. It was also estimated to be the 13th most valuable sports team in the world by Forbes in the same year.

Thanks especially to the Kop, the loudest section of the stadium, Anfield is known for having one of the best atmospheres in football. So it’s not surprising that many students coming to study in Liverpool, will be looking to go to some Liverpool F.C. matches.

If you want to live near Anfield, we list some excellent options here on Student.com. Phoenix Place offers private rooms and fully self-contained studio apartments about a 25-minute walk from Anfield. Alternatively you can get to the stadium in about 15 minutes by public transport. What’s more, Phoenix Place is only about a 10-minute walk from the Liverpool John Moores University city campus, so you can also get to your classes quickly and easily.

Another handy option for getting to Anfield is Atlantic Point. From there you can get to the stadium in about 35 minutes by walking or in 20 minutes by public transport. You’ll also be only a 5-minute walk away from Liverpool John Moores University’s city campus. Atlantic Point offers private en-suite rooms, meaning you’ll also have a private bathroom.

Student accommodation near Goodison Park

Goodison Park is the home of Everton F.C. The ground is famously close to Anfield, with the two stadiums being less than 1 kilometre apart, on opposite sides of Stanley Park. Goodison is slightly further away from the city centre though, making it a bit more challenging to reach on foot from the different student accommodation buildings in the city. Because of this it might be a better idea to live closer to the city centre, in an area with good transport links to the stadium.

Vita Student Liverpool has a great location in the city centre. Living there you’ll be right in the middle of all the city buzz, and can get to Goodison Park in about 20 minutes by public transport. You can also walk to the stadium if you want, but this will take about an hour. Vita Student Liverpool offers private rooms with shared bathrooms as well as fully private studio apartments.

Another great option is true Student Liverpool. From this student accommodation building you can get to Goodison Park in about 20 minutes by public transport or in about 45 minutes if you want to walk. You’ll also be only about a 10-minute walk away from the University of Liverpool, so getting to campus will be easy too. True Liverpool offers private en-suite rooms and fully self-contained studios.

These are some great options for football fans (and others) for accommodation in Liverpool, but it is always a good idea to check all the options you have available. You can do this by checking out all of the student accommodation in Liverpool that we list. We list dozens of options to choose from, so no matter what you’re looking for, you’ll surely find your ideal student home. If you’re looking to find out about the best student areas in Liverpool – this guide is for you! 

To help put this guide together, we spoke to two of our landlord partners, Meeta Padhiar from Galbraith Estates and Andrew Britton from iQ Student Accommodation.  

In no particular order, we’ve taken a look at the most popular areas and what makes them great.

Here are the four best student areas in Liverpool:

1. Wavertree

Wavertree is by far one of the most popular areas in Liverpool for students.

Because of its bustling student population, you’ll find plenty of shops, restaurants and bars here that offer great student deals.

An interesting fact about Wavertree is that its name comes from the Old English words ‘wæfre’ and ‘treow’, which mean “wavering tree”.

Needless to say, the area isn’t short of green spaces – like the Wavertree Botanic Gardens.

Meeta: “The popular, ever growing area of Wavertree consists of a diverse range of shops, restaurants and bars, right on your doorstep. It is nothing shy of culture and fun. A thriving local area catering for students living away from home. A great place to see, visit and spend time for both students and their families.”

Another highlight of Wavertree is that rents are, on average, cheaper than some of the more central areas in Liverpool.

If you don’t mind a 40 minute walk to university (20 minutes by bus), then you’ll love living in Wavertree.  

2. Liverpool University Area

Perhaps you’re not a huge fan of walking.

Well, fear not, there are plenty of accommodation options close to Liverpool’s universities.

What’s more, the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University are both reasonably close by.

So, if you’d like to live within walking distance of the city centre – this is the area for you!

Here, you’ll be close to sites like the World Museum, Walker Art Gallery and Central Library.

Liverpool Lime Street Station is just around the corner too!

Andrew: “The University of Liverpool city campus is a hive of activity where students can find most things they need, but there is so much more just a short walk away.”

Compare the best Liverpool student accommodation on Student.com.

3. Liverpool City Centre

Why not take full advantage of what Liverpool has to offer by living right in the city centre?

The majority of Liverpool’s shopping hotspots and famous landmarks are here – so chances are you’ll be in this area regularly.

Andrew: “In omission of the obvious tourist areas of the city, one area perfect for students is Bold Street where you’ll find dozens of unique retailers, world food stores, bars and restaurants most of which offer student discounts. On the streets running parallel to Bold Street in the Rope Walks District you can find many surprising hidden gems, including the FACT cinema and arts centre – definitely not your average cinema.”

The main drawback, as with any city centre location, is that rents here can be slightly higher compared to other areas.

4. Baltic Triangle

The Baltic Triangle is the place to be for creatives in Liverpool.  

The area is home to Liverpool’s creative businesses, as well as great restaurants, bars and live music venues.    

Living here, you’ll also find the city centre and areas like Chinatown within walking distance.  

Andrew: “The Baltic Triangle area of the city is fast becoming the cultural and creative centre of Liverpool with many of the old warehouse buildings undergoing transformation into conceptual venue spaces. Whatever you’re studying you’ll find something in the area that will inspire you!”

Check out our Liverpool student guide for tips on the best places to eat, shop and have fun.

Getting around

Liverpool has great transport options with a good network of buses, trains and ferries. The best place for information on routes, timetables, fares, passes and travel guides for Liverpool is the Merseytravel website. The site also regularly features special promotions and has a journey planner tool to help you navigate the city.

Cycling is a good way to get around and explore Liverpool, as well as being an excellent way to keep fit. Liverpool boasts the UK’s biggest bike hire service outside of London, Citybike, which offers 24-hour rentals from more than 130 stations across the city. Citybike also offers discounted student rates for their annual memberships and often run promotions at the start of university semesters.

Things to do

Liverpool was the European Capital of Culture in 2008 and is now a popular destination for visitors from around the world. From the Liverpool Echo Arena, a great venue for live music, to a fantastic sports scene, the city has so much for international students to experience.

If you’re keen to save money, there’s a wide range of activities on offer for free, or a very reasonable price.

Liverpool has more museums and galleries than any other UK city outside of London, and most of them are free to enter. A few of the most popular sites are the Museum of Liverpool, World Museum, Tate Liverpool and Walker Art Gallery – one of the oldest public art museums in the UK. For a full list of museums and galleries in Liverpool, check out the National Museums Liverpool website.

For music lovers, the Liverpool International Music Festival Summer Jam is a three-day outdoor music festival that attracts headline acts from around the world every year. The best thing about the festival is that it’s free to access!

Eating out

Liverpool is a great destination for passionate foodies. The city offers a diverse range of food options and some of the best international cuisine in the UK.

There are plenty of hidden gems dotted around the city and several areas that are popular with international students.

For some of the best Chinese restaurants in the UK, visit Liverpool’s Chinatown – home to one of the oldest overseas Chinese communities in Europe and almost 100 restaurants. Or for a truly picturesque dining experience, head over to the Albert Dock – a World Heritage Site waterfront featuring the UK’s largest collection of Grade I listed buildings.

Eating out doesn’t have to be pricey either. If you’re looking to eat out on a budget, there are plenty of inexpensive eats to sample in Liverpool. Here are a few recommendations to start you off on your gastronomic journey:

  • Bakchich

Bakchich offers Lebanese street food, a sensational blend of fresh and vibrant flavours. Perfect for both quick lunches and sit-down evening meals.

Address: 54 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4ER

  • Bellagio

Bellagio is one of the most popular places in Liverpool for traditional British fish and chips.

Address: Unit 15, The Colonnades, Albert Dock, Liverpool, L3 4AA

  • Big Bowl Noodle Bar

For a hearty bowl of noodles, Big Bowl Noodle Bar, as the name suggests, is the place to visit.

Address: 54 Berry Street, Liverpool, L1 4JF

  • Café Tabac

Café Tabac offers a cool, continental mix of coffee, cocktails and cinema, and a great selection of European food.

Address: 126 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4JA

  • Delkery

Delkery is a friendly, family-run café that serves fresh and quality handmade food and drinks.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • The Egg Café

The Egg Café is one of Liverpool’s best vegetarian and vegan restaurants. It’s located in a quaint old Victorian Warehouse and also serves as an independent art gallery.

Address: Top Floor, 16 – 18 Newington, Liverpool, L1 4ED

  • Lox & Caper

Located in the Merseyside Youth Association building, Lox & Caper has a great selection of good value food, all of which is prepared in-house.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • Tortilla

While Tortilla isn’t exclusive to Liverpool, it’s an excellent place for inexpensive tortillas and offers student discount.

Address: 70 Lord Street, Liverpool, L2 1TL

Shopping

For an ‘everything under one roof’ experience, check out Liverpool ONE. Liverpool ONE is the largest shopping complex in the city centre and the fifth largest in the UK. It’s host to a great selection of more than 170 shops, restaurants and bars and entertainment facilities.

Other shopping complexes worth checking out in Liverpool’s city centre are Metquarter Liverpool and St. Johns Shopping Centre.

Another shopping hotspot, especially for visitors is Liverpool’s Bold Street. Along the bustling high street, you’ll discover a range of boutiques and independent shops, as well as a mixture of big brand names.

Finding accommodation 

Finding a place to live in Liverpool can be daunting, especially if you’re looking from overseas.

The most popular areas are the City Centre, Wavertree, Liverpool University Area and the Baltic Triangle. As with most cities, average prices for accommodation in the city centre tend to be slightly higher than other areas.

Want to know more? Read our guide on the best student areas in Liverpool.

For the best selection of quality student accommodation in Liverpool, visit Student.com.

Title: Check out some of the best student accommodation in Liverpool
Content:
  If you’ve decided to study in Liverpool, whether for an exchange year or for your whole degree, you’ll need to find student accommodation. Finding the right accommodation for you in a city as big as Liverpool can be tricky, with lots of different options to choose from. To help you choose, we’ve listed four great student properties in this article. Check them out and maybe you’ll find the ideal student home for you! Liverpool cathedral is one of the most recognisable buildings in the city. Cambridge Court Living in Cambridge Court , you’ll be in the heart of Liverpool’s Knowledge Quarter, with both the city’s universities and its cultural scene right at your doorstep. You can walk to both the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University in under 10 minutes. You’ll also be in a central location, and will be able to walk to the city centre in about 15 minutes. Cambridge Court offers fully furnished private rooms with all bills included. true Liverpool This luxurious and modern student property offers private en-suite rooms and fully self-contained studio apartments. true Liverpool also has a great, central location, which means you can walk to the University of Liverpool as well as Liverpool John Moores University in less than 20 minutes. The property has amazing amenities including an in-house gym, a cinema room, an entertainment room and a dedicated study space. All bills, as well as cleaning service, are included in your rent. The Railyard Located in the Edge Hill neighbourhood of Liverpool, The Railyard is very close to the Liverpool Knowledge Quarter and the universities. You can walk to the University of Liverpool in about 10 minutes and to Liverpool John Moores University in 15. The fully furnished rooms are private with an en-suite bathroom. All bills are included in your rent. Prospect Point Prospect Point is located just north of Liverpool’s Knowledge Quarter, within walking distance of the universities and the city centre. You’ll also be living very close to several green spaces, such as Rupert Lane Recreation Ground. You can book a private room with an en-suite bathroom or a fully self-contained studio apartment. The rooms are fully furnished and all bills are included in the rent. These are just some of the student apartments we list in Liverpool. Currently we offer more than 60 student properties in the city. If you want to compare all of our accommodation options in Liverpool, you can check them out here .

If you’re looking for cheap student accommodation in Liverpool then you can start your search on this website or on our app. Make sure to also sign-up for a free account. This way a member of our bookings team can help you find the ideal student home just for you. One of the good things about Liverpool, compared to for example London, is that student accommodation is much cheaper on average. Especially the Liverpool John Moores University city campus is really close by, just a 5-minute walk away. In Atlantic Point you’ll live in a private en-suite room, meaning you’ll have a bedroom and a bathroom just for yourself. content.text:

URLs require status and redirect verification before citation.] Matches in posts page 3: [{"id":9168,"date":"2017-05-26T15:55:31","date_gmt":"2017-05-26T15:55:31","guid":{"rendered":"https://www.student.com/?p=9168"},"modified":"2025-02-27T11:29:09","modified_gmt":"2025-02-27T11:29:09","slug":"best-student-areas-liverpool","status":"publish","type":"post","link":"https://www.student.com/articles/best-student-areas-liverpool","title":{"rendered":"4 Best Student Areas in Liverpool"},"content":{"rendered":"

If you’re looking to find out about the best student areas in Liverpool – this guide is for you! 

To help put this guide together, we spoke to two of our landlord partners, Meeta Padhiar from Galbraith Estates and Andrew Britton from iQ Student Accommodation.  

In no particular order, we’ve taken a look at the most popular areas and what makes them great.

Here are the four best student areas in Liverpool:

1. Wavertree

Wavertree is by far one of the most popular areas in Liverpool for students.

Because of its bustling student population, you’ll find plenty of shops, restaurants and bars here that offer great student deals.

An interesting fact about Wavertree is that its name comes from the Old English words ‘wæfre’ and ‘treow’, which mean “wavering tree”.

Needless to say, the area isn’t short of green spaces – like the Wavertree Botanic Gardens.

Meeta: “The popular, ever growing area of Wavertree consists of a diverse range of shops, restaurants and bars, right on your doorstep. It is nothing shy of culture and fun. A thriving local area catering for students living away from home. A great place to see, visit and spend time for both students and their families.”

Another highlight of Wavertree is that rents are, on average, cheaper than some of the more central areas in Liverpool.

If you don’t mind a 40 minute walk to university (20 minutes by bus), then you’ll love living in Wavertree.  

2. Liverpool University Area

Perhaps you’re not a huge fan of walking.

Well, fear not, there are plenty of accommodation options close to Liverpool’s universities.

What’s more, the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University are both reasonably close by.

So, if you’d like to live within walking distance of the city centre – this is the area for you!

Here, you’ll be close to sites like the World Museum, Walker Art Gallery and Central Library.

Liverpool Lime Street Station is just around the corner too!

Andrew: “The University of Liverpool city campus is a hive of activity where students can find most things they need, but there is so much more just a short walk away.”

Compare the best Liverpool student accommodation on Student.com.

3. Liverpool City Centre

Why not take full advantage of what Liverpool has to offer by living right in the city centre?

The majority of Liverpool’s shopping hotspots and famous landmarks are here – so chances are you’ll be in this area regularly.

Andrew: “In omission of the obvious tourist areas of the city, one area perfect for students is Bold Street where you’ll find dozens of unique retailers, world food stores, bars and restaurants most of which offer student discounts. On the streets running parallel to Bold Street in the Rope Walks District you can find many surprising hidden gems, including the FACT cinema and arts centre – definitely not your average cinema.”

The main drawback, as with any city centre location, is that rents here can be slightly higher compared to other areas.

4. Baltic Triangle

The Baltic Triangle is the place to be for creatives in Liverpool.  

The area is home to Liverpool’s creative businesses, as well as great restaurants, bars and live music venues.    

Living here, you’ll also find the city centre and areas like Chinatown within walking distance.  

Andrew: “The Baltic Triangle area of the city is fast becoming the cultural and creative centre of Liverpool with many of the old warehouse buildings undergoing transformation into conceptual venue spaces. Whatever you’re studying you’ll find something in the area that will inspire you!”

Check out our Liverpool student guide for tips on the best places to eat, shop and have fun.

Getting around

Liverpool has great transport options with a good network of buses, trains and ferries. The best place for information on routes, timetables, fares, passes and travel guides for Liverpool is the Merseytravel website. The site also regularly features special promotions and has a journey planner tool to help you navigate the city.

Cycling is a good way to get around and explore Liverpool, as well as being an excellent way to keep fit. Liverpool boasts the UK’s biggest bike hire service outside of London, Citybike, which offers 24-hour rentals from more than 130 stations across the city. Citybike also offers discounted student rates for their annual memberships and often run promotions at the start of university semesters.

Things to do

Liverpool was the European Capital of Culture in 2008 and is now a popular destination for visitors from around the world. From the Liverpool Echo Arena, a great venue for live music, to a fantastic sports scene, the city has so much for international students to experience.

If you’re keen to save money, there’s a wide range of activities on offer for free, or a very reasonable price.

Liverpool has more museums and galleries than any other UK city outside of London, and most of them are free to enter. A few of the most popular sites are the Museum of Liverpool, World Museum, Tate Liverpool and Walker Art Gallery – one of the oldest public art museums in the UK. For a full list of museums and galleries in Liverpool, check out the National Museums Liverpool website.

For music lovers, the Liverpool International Music Festival Summer Jam is a three-day outdoor music festival that attracts headline acts from around the world every year. The best thing about the festival is that it’s free to access!

Eating out

Liverpool is a great destination for passionate foodies. The city offers a diverse range of food options and some of the best international cuisine in the UK.

There are plenty of hidden gems dotted around the city and several areas that are popular with international students.

For some of the best Chinese restaurants in the UK, visit Liverpool’s Chinatown – home to one of the oldest overseas Chinese communities in Europe and almost 100 restaurants. Or for a truly picturesque dining experience, head over to the Albert Dock – a World Heritage Site waterfront featuring the UK’s largest collection of Grade I listed buildings.

Eating out doesn’t have to be pricey either. If you’re looking to eat out on a budget, there are plenty of inexpensive eats to sample in Liverpool. Here are a few recommendations to start you off on your gastronomic journey:

  • Bakchich

Bakchich offers Lebanese street food, a sensational blend of fresh and vibrant flavours. Perfect for both quick lunches and sit-down evening meals.

Address: 54 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4ER

  • Bellagio

Bellagio is one of the most popular places in Liverpool for traditional British fish and chips.

Address: Unit 15, The Colonnades, Albert Dock, Liverpool, L3 4AA

  • Big Bowl Noodle Bar

For a hearty bowl of noodles, Big Bowl Noodle Bar, as the name suggests, is the place to visit.

Address: 54 Berry Street, Liverpool, L1 4JF

  • Café Tabac

Café Tabac offers a cool, continental mix of coffee, cocktails and cinema, and a great selection of European food.

Address: 126 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4JA

  • Delkery

Delkery is a friendly, family-run café that serves fresh and quality handmade food and drinks.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • The Egg Café

The Egg Café is one of Liverpool’s best vegetarian and vegan restaurants. It’s located in a quaint old Victorian Warehouse and also serves as an independent art gallery.

Address: Top Floor, 16 – 18 Newington, Liverpool, L1 4ED

  • Lox & Caper

Located in the Merseyside Youth Association building, Lox & Caper has a great selection of good value food, all of which is prepared in-house.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • Tortilla

While Tortilla isn’t exclusive to Liverpool, it’s an excellent place for inexpensive tortillas and offers student discount.

Address: 70 Lord Street, Liverpool, L2 1TL

Shopping

For an ‘everything under one roof’ experience, check out Liverpool ONE. Liverpool ONE is the largest shopping complex in the city centre and the fifth largest in the UK. It’s host to a great selection of more than 170 shops, restaurants and bars and entertainment facilities.

Other shopping complexes worth checking out in Liverpool’s city centre are Metquarter Liverpool and St. Johns Shopping Centre.

Another shopping hotspot, especially for visitors is Liverpool’s Bold Street. Along the bustling high street, you’ll discover a range of boutiques and independent shops, as well as a mixture of big brand names.

Finding accommodation 

Finding a place to live in Liverpool can be daunting, especially if you’re looking from overseas.

The most popular areas are the City Centre, Wavertree, Liverpool University Area and the Baltic Triangle. As with most cities, average prices for accommodation in the city centre tend to be slightly higher than other areas.

Want to know more? Read our guide on the best student areas in Liverpool.

For the best selection of quality student accommodation in Liverpool, visit Student.com.

Liverpool is a great city for university students. It’s a fun city with lots of interesting things to do, and most importantly for prospective students, it’s home to a couple of very good universities. If you’re looking for cheap student accommodation in Liverpool then you can start your search on this website or on our app. Make sure to also sign-up for a free account. This way a member of our bookings team can help you find the ideal student home just for you.

One of the good things about Liverpool, compared to for example London, is that student accommodation is much cheaper on average. You can find some really good student properties that won’t break the bank but are still in good locations, near universities and the city centre. In this post we’ve listed some of the most popular options for cheap student accommodation in Liverpool.

Atlantic Point

Atlantic Point is in a great location near the city centre. This means you’ll have great shopping and nightlife options right at your doorstep, in addition to being able to get to your campus quickly. Especially the Liverpool John Moores University city campus is really close by, just a 5-minute walk away. In Atlantic Point you’ll live in a private en-suite room, meaning you’ll have a bedroom and a bathroom just for yourself. The rooms are fully furnished and the property facilities include an entertainment room, a communal laundry room and bike storage. Prices start from £107/week.

Grand Central

As the name suggests, you’ll be in a very central location at the Grand Central. Just over a 5-minute walk to Liverpool John Moores University and about 15 minutes on foot to the University of Liverpool, you’ll also be right next to Liverpool Lime Street and Liverpool Central stations. Grand Central is equipped with airy rooms, fresh decor and laundry facilities, meaning you can quickly make this place feel like a home when you study in Liverpool. There are several options for how you want to live, with private rooms with shared bathrooms, private rooms with en-suite bathroom and fully self-contained studio apartments all on offer. Prices start from £105/week.

Agnes Jones House

Located in Liverpool’s Georgian Quarter, Agnes Jones House is about a 10-minute walk from both the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University. With prices starting at just £85/week, this is the perfect property for a student looking for a cheap, convenient home away from home at university. With an entertainment room, bike storage and laundry, everything you need is on-site.

St Andrew’s Gardens

St Andrew’s Gardens is the cheapest accommodation we currently list in Liverpool, with prices starting at just £84/week. Even at this price you’ll still be within walking distance of your campus. You can walk to Liverpool John Moores University in about 5 minutes and to the University of Liverpool in 10 minutes. You’ll get to live in a private bedroom, and depending on the room you choose, your bathroom can be either shared or private. All bills are included in the price as well.

Falkland House

Falkland House has a great location near the Royal Liverpool University Hospital. You can walk to Liverpool John Moores University in 10 minutes and to the University of Liverpool in under 15. The rooms are fully furnished and all bills, including Wi-Fi, are included in the rent. The facilities include a bike storage, entertainment room and communal laundry. You’ll also be in a safe environment with an onsite manager and a security officer always on-site. Prices start from £118/week.

All prices are correct as of 15th February 2023. For full details please refer to the property page listing on Student.com or contact a member of the team for confirmation of pricing. Our bookings team are always happy to answer any questions you may have and help you find the ideal student home for you.

Liverpool is home to Liverpool F.C. and Everton F.C. and is one of the most passionate football cities in the country. Both Liverpool and Everton are historically successful clubs with Liverpool having claimed 19 English league titles and six Champions League titles, and Everton having been champions of England nine times. Especially Liverpool is one of the most widely supported teams in the world, with lots of fans in all corners of the globe.

Liverpool, hometown of the legendary Beatles, is a city and metropolitan borough in Merseyside, England. This iconic city has a lot more to offer than football and one of the most influential bands of all time though. With a grand backdrop of Victorian and Georgian buildings, it’s an intimate and vibrant city that celebrates its glorious past. It’s home to many famous landmarks such as the homes of The Beatles members, The Liver Buildings, and the historic docks – all of which will become familiar sights if you choose to study in the city.

Still, for a football fan, the beautiful game is definitely one of the biggest draws of the city. In this post we list some great options for student accommodation for anyone who’s coming to study in Liverpool and is interested in seeing some games.

Student accommodation near Anfield

Anfield is one of the most legendary stadiums in the world. The team’s passionate fans, The Kop stand behind one of the goals and the singing of You’ll Never Walk Alone before every home game are things every football fan knows about. Liverpool has tens of millions of fans all over the world and it was 7th in the Deloitte Football Money League in 2022, meaning it is the 7th richest football club in the world. It was also estimated to be the 13th most valuable sports team in the world by Forbes in the same year.

Thanks especially to the Kop, the loudest section of the stadium, Anfield is known for having one of the best atmospheres in football. So it’s not surprising that many students coming to study in Liverpool, will be looking to go to some Liverpool F.C. matches.

If you want to live near Anfield, we list some excellent options here on Student.com. Phoenix Place offers private rooms and fully self-contained studio apartments about a 25-minute walk from Anfield. Alternatively you can get to the stadium in about 15 minutes by public transport. What’s more, Phoenix Place is only about a 10-minute walk from the Liverpool John Moores University city campus, so you can also get to your classes quickly and easily.

Another handy option for getting to Anfield is Atlantic Point. From there you can get to the stadium in about 35 minutes by walking or in 20 minutes by public transport. You’ll also be only a 5-minute walk away from Liverpool John Moores University’s city campus. Atlantic Point offers private en-suite rooms, meaning you’ll also have a private bathroom.

Student accommodation near Goodison Park

Goodison Park is the home of Everton F.C. The ground is famously close to Anfield, with the two stadiums being less than 1 kilometre apart, on opposite sides of Stanley Park. Goodison is slightly further away from the city centre though, making it a bit more challenging to reach on foot from the different student accommodation buildings in the city. Because of this it might be a better idea to live closer to the city centre, in an area with good transport links to the stadium.

Vita Student Liverpool has a great location in the city centre. Living there you’ll be right in the middle of all the city buzz, and can get to Goodison Park in about 20 minutes by public transport. You can also walk to the stadium if you want, but this will take about an hour. Vita Student Liverpool offers private rooms with shared bathrooms as well as fully private studio apartments.

Another great option is true Student Liverpool. From this student accommodation building you can get to Goodison Park in about 20 minutes by public transport or in about 45 minutes if you want to walk. You’ll also be only about a 10-minute walk away from the University of Liverpool, so getting to campus will be easy too. True Liverpool offers private en-suite rooms and fully self-contained studios.

These are some great options for football fans (and others) for accommodation in Liverpool, but it is always a good idea to check all the options you have available. You can do this by checking out all of the student accommodation in Liverpool that we list. We list dozens of options to choose from, so no matter what you’re looking for, you’ll surely find your ideal student home. Make sure to create an account with us so that our booking consultants can get in touch and help you find the ideal student accommodation just for you!

If you’re looking to find out about the best student areas in Liverpool – this guide is for you! 

To help put this guide together, we spoke to two of our landlord partners, Meeta Padhiar from Galbraith Estates and Andrew Britton from iQ Student Accommodation.  

In no particular order, we’ve taken a look at the most popular areas and what makes them great.

Here are the four best student areas in Liverpool:

1. Wavertree

Wavertree is by far one of the most popular areas in Liverpool for students.

Because of its bustling student population, you’ll find plenty of shops, restaurants and bars here that offer great student deals.

An interesting fact about Wavertree is that its name comes from the Old English words ‘wæfre’ and ‘treow’, which mean “wavering tree”.

Needless to say, the area isn’t short of green spaces – like the Wavertree Botanic Gardens.

Meeta: “The popular, ever growing area of Wavertree consists of a diverse range of shops, restaurants and bars, right on your doorstep. It is nothing shy of culture and fun. A thriving local area catering for students living away from home. A great place to see, visit and spend time for both students and their families.”

Another highlight of Wavertree is that rents are, on average, cheaper than some of the more central areas in Liverpool.

If you don’t mind a 40 minute walk to university (20 minutes by bus), then you’ll love living in Wavertree.  

2. Liverpool University Area

Perhaps you’re not a huge fan of walking.

Well, fear not, there are plenty of accommodation options close to Liverpool’s universities.

What’s more, the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University are both reasonably close by.

So, if you’d like to live within walking distance of the city centre – this is the area for you!

Here, you’ll be close to sites like the World Museum, Walker Art Gallery and Central Library.

Liverpool Lime Street Station is just around the corner too!

Andrew: “The University of Liverpool city campus is a hive of activity where students can find most things they need, but there is so much more just a short walk away.”

Compare the best Liverpool student accommodation on Student.com.

3. Liverpool City Centre

Why not take full advantage of what Liverpool has to offer by living right in the city centre?

The majority of Liverpool’s shopping hotspots and famous landmarks are here – so chances are you’ll be in this area regularly.

Andrew: “In omission of the obvious tourist areas of the city, one area perfect for students is Bold Street where you’ll find dozens of unique retailers, world food stores, bars and restaurants most of which offer student discounts. On the streets running parallel to Bold Street in the Rope Walks District you can find many surprising hidden gems, including the FACT cinema and arts centre – definitely not your average cinema.”

The main drawback, as with any city centre location, is that rents here can be slightly higher compared to other areas.

4. Baltic Triangle

The Baltic Triangle is the place to be for creatives in Liverpool.  

The area is home to Liverpool’s creative businesses, as well as great restaurants, bars and live music venues.    

Living here, you’ll also find the city centre and areas like Chinatown within walking distance.  

Andrew: “The Baltic Triangle area of the city is fast becoming the cultural and creative centre of Liverpool with many of the old warehouse buildings undergoing transformation into conceptual venue spaces. Whatever you’re studying you’ll find something in the area that will inspire you!”

Check out our Liverpool student guide for tips on the best places to eat, shop and have fun.

Getting around

Liverpool has great transport options with a good network of buses, trains and ferries. The best place for information on routes, timetables, fares, passes and travel guides for Liverpool is the Merseytravel website. The site also regularly features special promotions and has a journey planner tool to help you navigate the city.

Cycling is a good way to get around and explore Liverpool, as well as being an excellent way to keep fit. Liverpool boasts the UK’s biggest bike hire service outside of London, Citybike, which offers 24-hour rentals from more than 130 stations across the city. Citybike also offers discounted student rates for their annual memberships and often run promotions at the start of university semesters.

Things to do

Liverpool was the European Capital of Culture in 2008 and is now a popular destination for visitors from around the world. From the Liverpool Echo Arena, a great venue for live music, to a fantastic sports scene, the city has so much for international students to experience.

If you’re keen to save money, there’s a wide range of activities on offer for free, or a very reasonable price.

Liverpool has more museums and galleries than any other UK city outside of London, and most of them are free to enter. A few of the most popular sites are the Museum of Liverpool, World Museum, Tate Liverpool and Walker Art Gallery – one of the oldest public art museums in the UK. For a full list of museums and galleries in Liverpool, check out the National Museums Liverpool website.

For music lovers, the Liverpool International Music Festival Summer Jam is a three-day outdoor music festival that attracts headline acts from around the world every year. The best thing about the festival is that it’s free to access!

Eating out

Liverpool is a great destination for passionate foodies. The city offers a diverse range of food options and some of the best international cuisine in the UK.

There are plenty of hidden gems dotted around the city and several areas that are popular with international students.

For some of the best Chinese restaurants in the UK, visit Liverpool’s Chinatown – home to one of the oldest overseas Chinese communities in Europe and almost 100 restaurants. Or for a truly picturesque dining experience, head over to the Albert Dock – a World Heritage Site waterfront featuring the UK’s largest collection of Grade I listed buildings.

Eating out doesn’t have to be pricey either. If you’re looking to eat out on a budget, there are plenty of inexpensive eats to sample in Liverpool. Here are a few recommendations to start you off on your gastronomic journey:

  • Bakchich

Bakchich offers Lebanese street food, a sensational blend of fresh and vibrant flavours. Perfect for both quick lunches and sit-down evening meals.

Address: 54 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4ER

  • Bellagio

Bellagio is one of the most popular places in Liverpool for traditional British fish and chips.

Address: Unit 15, The Colonnades, Albert Dock, Liverpool, L3 4AA

  • Big Bowl Noodle Bar

For a hearty bowl of noodles, Big Bowl Noodle Bar, as the name suggests, is the place to visit.

Address: 54 Berry Street, Liverpool, L1 4JF

  • Café Tabac

Café Tabac offers a cool, continental mix of coffee, cocktails and cinema, and a great selection of European food.

Address: 126 Bold Street, Liverpool, L1 4JA

  • Delkery

Delkery is a friendly, family-run café that serves fresh and quality handmade food and drinks.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • The Egg Café

The Egg Café is one of Liverpool’s best vegetarian and vegan restaurants. It’s located in a quaint old Victorian Warehouse and also serves as an independent art gallery.

Address: Top Floor, 16 – 18 Newington, Liverpool, L1 4ED

  • Lox & Caper

Located in the Merseyside Youth Association building, Lox & Caper has a great selection of good value food, all of which is prepared in-house.

Address: Unit 3, Westminster Chambers, 90-98 Dale Street, Liverpool, L2 5TF

  • Tortilla

While Tortilla isn’t exclusive to Liverpool, it’s an excellent place for inexpensive tortillas and offers student discount.

Address: 70 Lord Street, Liverpool, L2 1TL

Shopping

For an ‘everything under one roof’ experience, check out Liverpool ONE. Liverpool ONE is the largest shopping complex in the city centre and the fifth largest in the UK. It’s host to a great selection of more than 170 shops, restaurants and bars and entertainment facilities.

Other shopping complexes worth checking out in Liverpool’s city centre are Metquarter Liverpool and St. Johns Shopping Centre.

Another shopping hotspot, especially for visitors is Liverpool’s Bold Street. Along the bustling high street, you’ll discover a range of boutiques and independent shops, as well as a mixture of big brand names.

Finding accommodation 

Finding a place to live in Liverpool can be daunting, especially if you’re looking from overseas.

The most popular areas are the City Centre, Wavertree, Liverpool University Area and the Baltic Triangle. As with most cities, average prices for accommodation in the city centre tend to be slightly higher than other areas.

Want to know more? Read our guide on the best student areas in Liverpool.

For the best selection of quality student accommodation in Liverpool, visit Student.com.

Title: Check out some of the best student accommodation in Liverpool
Content:
  If you’ve decided to study in Liverpool, whether for an exchange year or for your whole degree, you’ll need to find student accommodation. Finding the right accommodation for you in a city as big as Liverpool can be tricky, with lots of different options to choose from. To help you choose, we’ve listed four great student properties in this article. Check them out and maybe you’ll find the ideal student home for you! Liverpool cathedral is one of the most recognisable buildings in the city. Cambridge Court Living in Cambridge Court , you’ll be in the heart of Liverpool’s Knowledge Quarter, with both the city’s universities and its cultural scene right at your doorstep. You can walk to both the University of Liverpool and Liverpool John Moores University in under 10 minutes. You’ll also be in a central location, and will be able to walk to the city centre in about 15 minutes. Cambridge Court offers fully furnished private rooms with all bills included. true Liverpool This luxurious and modern student property offers private en-suite rooms and fully self-contained studio apartments. true Liverpool also has a great, central location, which means you can walk to the University of Liverpool as well as Liverpool John Moores University in less than 20 minutes. The property has amazing amenities including an in-house gym, a cinema room, an entertainment room and a dedicated study space. All bills, as well as cleaning service, are included in your rent. The Railyard Located in the Edge Hill neighbourhood of Liverpool, The Railyard is very close to the Liverpool Knowledge Quarter and the universities. You can walk to the University of Liverpool in about 10 minutes and to Liverpool John Moores University in 15. The fully furnished rooms are private with an en-suite bathroom. All bills are included in your rent. Prospect Point Prospect Point is located just north of Liverpool’s Knowledge Quarter, within walking distance of the universities and the city centre. You’ll also be living very close to several green spaces, such as Rupert Lane Recreation Ground. You can book a private room with an en-suite bathroom or a fully self-contained studio apartment. The rooms are fully furnished and all bills are included in the rent. These are just some of the student apartments we list in Liverpool. Currently we offer more than 60 student properties in the city. If you want to compare all of our accommodation options in Liverpool, you can check them out here .
